title: Stop Listening to This Terrible LinkedIn Advice
description:
It’s time to stop believing this myth:

Messaging a recruiter will NOT get you “blacklisted.”

Will sending generic messages hurt you? It could...

But one thoughtful, relevant message after you apply can actually help you stand out.

Here’s what to do instead:

Mention the job title (and req # if available)
Share 1–2 sentences on how you solve the problem the role is hiring for
Ask one thoughtful, relevant question

That’s it.

Visibility matters in this market.
And the job seekers getting interviews? They’re not staying invisible.

transcript: It is time to cut the crap, and yes, I am talking about you, random person on LinkedIn who just told all job seekers that if they ever send a DM to a recruiter, they're going to be on some magical blacklist in which recruiters will never reach out to them again. Look, it's not helpful to blow up recruiters' inboxes with messages such as, "I applied to your job. I've attached my resume." Or, "Do you have any roles you can refer me to?" However, one thoughtful communication after you've applied to a job, just briefly giving the job title, the job requisition number, one to two really brief sentences about how you solve the problem that role was meant to solve, and maybe one really insightful question about the job, that could really set you apart. Visibility matters in this market. If you want to follow someone who's going to give you the real job search tips and no BS, follow me.
